citations.check: OK  §1985:IV.1 p1  (1. INTRODUCTION)  the text is in p1

citations.quote: Qualification is not included in level 1
citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.1.3.2 p1  (1.3.2 Name Characteristics)  the text is in p1

cases.reason: S1 ('The language considerations and rules specified in this section, apply to the highest level') states the scope of the section's text; the rules themselves are their own rows. S2 ('the restrictions will be pointed out in the section describing that language element') describes where the document places level restrictions. S3 ('specifications unique to the high level are enclosed in boxes') describes the document's notation. S4 ('restrictions contained in one module might possibly affect other modules') informs the reader about how the module descriptions interact. S5 restates a requirement as an example: 'qualification is not allowed in level 1 of the Nucleus' is carried by 1985-SR-VI.1.3.2-p1 ('Qualification is not included in level 1', cite.py OK §1985:VI.1.3.2 p1); its consequence for a module combined with Nucleus level 1 is that row applied to the combination, and the row is tested there. S6 ('The flowcharts in this document ... are not meant to dictate implementation') describes the figures and grants the implementor freedom: every compiler behaviour satisfies it. No sentence other than S5 says anything of a program or a compiler, and S5's requirement has its own row. Restated requirements, each its own row: "qualification is not allowed in level 1 of the Nucleus" is 1985-SR-VI.1.3.2-p1.
cases.compiler-at-1985: not probed: the text is about the standard's own presentation, not a program or an obligation on the implementation
cases.needs: a signed derivation (the informative arm, kb/Work PB6012)

derivation.names: describes the standard's scope of Section IV, its boxes and its flowcharts: "specifications unique to the high level are enclosed in boxes"

Neither sentence requires any layout or result; an object program that uses extra operations, or none, is consistent with both 'may' statements, and no program's output can show the count of machine operations. The SYNCHRONIZED requirements are their own rows (p3, -1, -2, p5 and the SYNCHRONIZED clause rows).

cases.attempt: S4/S5: a --std 85 program qualifying a name (e.g. a record field OF a file record) under a module combined with Nucleus level 1, accepted by the compiler; S1: a high-level construct rejected as outside 'the highest level'; S3: a boxed (level-2) element mishandled.
cases.reason: S5's restriction is carried by 1985-SR-VI.1.3.2-p1 (exists; cite.py OK 'Qualification is not included in level 1'), and qualification is a Nucleus facility, so its absence in a level-1 combination is that row applied to the combination; S4 ('restrictions contained in one module might possibly affect other modules', cite.py OK) only announces S5. The compiler implements the high level, where no level-1 restriction applies, so no behaviour of it can contradict S1-S4. S3 is notation (the catalog's box field derives from it, a transcription matter, not compiler behaviour). S6 grants freedom. All three quotations OK in p1.

cases.attempt: Read the list as a constraint on source text: a clause containing an element outside the list (e.g. a picture string or literal) would then be illegal, or a compiler accepting such text would break it.
cases.reason: The list names brackets, braces and lowercase words, which never occur in source text, so the sentence can only be about how the document writes a general format; the element kinds' source-text consequences are their own rows (1985-SR-IV.2.1.2-p1, 1985-SR-IV.2.1.7-p1 and the others named exist). The SR kind label does not make the enumeration falsifiable. Quote OK in p1.

cases.attempt: A program using an ellipsis-repeated format element (e.g. MOVE x TO y z w) accepted or rejected by the compiler.
cases.reason: S1 is limited to 'text, other than general formats', i.e. the standard's prose; the general-format ellipsis is 1985-SR-IV.2.1.5-p2/-p3 (exist). Quote OK.

cases.attempt: S2 'relax restrictions implied by words or elements': a compiler that enforces a format restriction an SR relaxes.
cases.reason: That error is a violation of the relaxing SR itself, not of this sentence, which only says SRs may do so. Both sentences classify the document's rules. Quote OK.

cases.attempt: A compiler whose effect on compilation or execution differs from a GR.
cases.reason: Such a defect falsifies that GR, not this definition of what a GR is. Quote OK.

cases.attempt: (a) Read 'may be facilitated if ... aligned' as obliging alignment of arithmetic or subscript operands; (b) a program whose output depends on whether straddling items cost extra machine operations; (c) unaligned non-SYNC data computed wrongly.
cases.reason: (a) 'may be facilitated' states possible efficiency, and p1 says storage 'need not respect these natural boundaries'; (b) no COBOL output exposes a count of machine operations; (c) correctness of unaligned data is p1 plus the data rows, not this sentence. S2 supplies the referent of 'such additional machine operations' in 1985-GR-IV.4.3.7-p3 (exists; cite.py OK 'are defined to be synchronized'), so 'explains' names a real row; the observable SYNCHRONIZED effects (implicit FILLER, group results) are p5 and the SYNC clause rows. Quotes OK in p2 and p3.

cases.attempt: An evaluation order differing from the figures, or a figure disagreeing with the rules.
cases.reason: S2 says the figures do not dictate implementation; the order requirements are 1985-GR-VI.6.3.4-p1/-1/-2 (exist). Quote OK.

cases.attempt: Any ROUNDED / SIZE ERROR / CORRESPONDING behaviour.
cases.reason: The sentence states only what paragraph 6.4 contains; each option is its own VI.6.4.x row. Quote OK.

cases.attempt: S2: an RWCS that applies body-group rules to a CF group differently from a DE group.
cases.reason: The joint treatment is restated as a requirement in 1985-GR-XIII.3.10.8-p1 (exists; cite.py OK 'points to the appropriate presentation rules for all permissible combinations'), whose rules -1..-6 name control heading, detail and control footing groups; S1 and S3 are organization and a page cross-reference. Quotes OK.

cases.attempt: S2: a report with no PAGE clause where the RWCS applies the PAGE-present rules (e.g. a report heading R / relative, first print line by 3b instead of 3d).
cases.reason: The selection is stated by the tables themselves: Table 1's header reads 'If the PAGE clause is specified.' / 'If the PAGE clause is omitted.' S2 is the legend for those column headers and adds no rule. Quote OK.

cases.reason: The permissible combinations are listed by the tables (1985-GR-XIII.3.10.2-p2 'list all of the permissible combinations'), and the abbreviations by 1985-GR-XIII.3.10.3-1/-2/-3/-p2 (exist); this sentence only announces the notation. Quote OK.
